lesson_title: Assembling with Instructions: Diagrams, Parts Lists and the Plug Wired Wrong
hook_text: The kettle boils. The plug is wired WRONG. And nothing in your kitchen will tell you — here's the check that will.
clip_script: Flat-pack bookshelf, ninety pieces, no sentences — just pictures giving orders. The exploded view floats every part where it belongs; dotted lines run from screw to hole. Before you build: roll call. Sixteen cam locks on the list, fourteen in the box? Two missing — three shelves lock, the fourth waits, and you found out BEFORE step 9 ate your afternoon. Now the order. Nail the back panel on early and the shelves have no door left to slide through. That thin back panel is also what keeps the frame square — skip it and your bookshelf leans like it's tired. Steps that seal go LAST. Now the plug, where order becomes safety. Brown to live, right. Blue to neutral, left. Green-and-yellow to earth, the tall pin on top. Swap brown and blue and here's the horror: the kettle still boils. Everything looks fine. But the switch is on the wrong wire now — the element stays LIVE with the switch off, waiting. Working is not the same as right. Check the colours, not the kettle. And the money? Self-assembly saves R320 — if you have the four hands step 7 demands. A cracked panel costs R380. Do that maths before the Allen key comes out.
visual_style: An exploded bookshelf hanging in mid-air over a kitchen table, parts clicking home along dotted lines; a parts list ticking itself; then an open plug in close-up, the brown and blue wires swapping with a red warning glow while the kettle steams innocently.
mood: Hands-on and quietly serious — DIY swagger that turns protective at the plug.
pacing: Playful through the roll call and the leaning bookshelf, then slowing hard at the plug for the safety reveal, closing quick on the R320-versus-R380 decision.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build anything the box throws at you — safely and in order.
